_help.about: Pocket worlds: Torchfire 1 is a set of bounded slices, one per biome, each with its ruins above and its dungeon below, joined underground and seen on each other's horizons. Not the planet (§CR is Torchfire 2). First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct, except where marked Mike; the designer owns them. Built 9 Oct (Claude Code, queue 71; Surface, surface below): the tomb's world's surface, the one world built so far: its size and edge, the one clock, its life and its layered horizon, as the lines below say. Not built yet: links (the passages between worlds, §EW.3), map (§EW.4, §FM.8: reference only, not built), every other world, and horizon.far_landmarks (§EW.7 steps 3 and 4).
_help.size: §EW.1. across_m: a world's size [min, max] (Claude's first guess, open for Mike). edge: the land itself closes a world (cliffs, water, thick forest, mountains); invisible_walls: never (§DM). Built 9 Oct (queue 71) for the tomb's world: surface.across_m wide, within across_m; the land closes it (SurfaceGround: a bajada under an escarpment ring, steeper than anything you can walk, cliff_m), never an invisible wall.
_help.clock: §EW.1; §FK.3 (7 Oct, answers §EW.8 call 2). The 144-minute day runs in every world (sky/day_cycle.json), the same everywhere: day 60, dusk 18, night 48, dawn 18. shared: one clock for all worlds. day_length_from_latitude: false (§FK.3; was Claude's guess, true): no latitude, no axial tilt, no year in Torchfire 1, so the tundra and the desert share one sunset; latitude: none. The moon's phases (§DD) count days and are untouched. axial_tilt_deg and year_days in day_cycle.json stay for the open world (Torchfire 2). Built (queues 61, 63 and 71): the crawler turns World.days at 144 minutes, and the surface's sky (SkySystem.one_clock: DayCycle's reference day, the sun rising due east, overhead at noon, setting due west) reads that same World.days, as the shafts below do (Vents.sun_deg): one clock, never a copy.
_help.life: §EW.1. plants: the biome's species by their real silhouettes (data/biomes, habitat.json; §CS: a forest is mostly one species). creatures: ambient sightings from the ecology's archetypes (data/creatures), going about their lives; population_sim: false (§ET.2, §EW.6). Built 9 Oct (queue 71) for the surface: its plants from the world's biome file (its associations in surface.realm: SurfacePlants), its creatures from data/creatures by the biome's climate (ground and ambient only, never a hunter: SurfaceLife); population_sim stays false.
_help.links: §EW.3 (Mike): worlds are loosely connected; you go underground in one and come out in another. by: underground. passage: what hides the load (Claude's first guess). loading_screen_ok: true (Mike): allowed where it can't be hidden. continuous_map: false: each world loads on its own.
_help.map: §EW.4 (Mike): an overworld map with fast travel to worlds already visited. from_to: hearth_to_hearth is Claude's first guess (leave one relit flame, borrow the next, §AW, §CQ), open for Mike.
_help.generation: Mike, 7 Oct: every world, its dungeon and its ruins are generated by rules, unique to each playthrough, and kept for good once rolled (answers §EW.8 call 7 and §ET.10 call 3). seed: one_per_new_game, every world and dungeon drawn from it. by: rules_per_kind, each kind of world, ruin and dungeon has its own rules (kits §CJ.8, plan §EX.2, one stone §EX.1, composition §EF, §EG). composed_by_hand: false (Mike's 'handcrafted' read as composed by rules). kept: true, relit stays relit, restored stays restored, gates keep their state (crawler.json persistence). map_holds: found, only worlds and dungeons you reached on foot (§FK.4, §EW.4). shot_check: Claude's suggestion, NOT locked (§FK.5 call 1): a world kind's check fails a seed whose first view on arrival ends on nothing. Built 9 Oct (Claude Code, queue 63; CrawlerSave), for the one world there is, the tomb's: seed: a new game rolls one and its dungeons come from it (crawler.json persistence: the first from the game's own seed, each next one the way out leads to from the game's seed and its place), the same tombs every time for that game. kept: true, a save per game (user://crawler/<game seed>.json): the dungeon you are in and the holders you relit in each, lit again on Continue; gates keep their state once gates exist. by: rules_per_kind, the tomb kit and its plan as built. Not built yet: map_holds (no map), shot_check (not locked), and every world but the tomb's (§EW.7).
_help.horizon: §EW.5. Near ground wholly this world's biome; farther out the land changes and fades lighter and bluer (R-rules). layers: near (this world's real ground), mid (impostors of this world's edge and the neighbours' landmarks, §ES.3), far (a painted band and the sky). far_landmarks: the other worlds' landmarks, so the peak you see is a place you can go (Mike); a world's neighbours sit in believable directions (§EW.8 call 6, Claude's guess). Built 9 Oct (queue 71) for the surface: near the basin's ground, mid the escarpment ring and its landmark butte (real ground, not impostors), far the band of ranges (surface.far_band) in the haze, and the sky. far_landmarks (the other worlds' landmarks) not built yet: there is no other world.
_help.worlds: §EW.2. Mike's named worlds, then every biome gets one (every_biome). name; biome: a data/biomes id (Claude's first pick, open where marked); mike: what Mike said of it; theme: the crawler.json theme that belongs to it, if any; status: named (only named so far; each is talked through on its own before it is locked). worlds.desert is the tomb's world (surface.world, queue 71, Claude Code's reading of §EY's snake and Mike's 'read today's tomb as a desert dungeon'; §FM.3's Aztec world against it is §FM.10 call 1): its biome grows the surface. Its theme stays open (FittedStone reads it for the tomb's own climate, damp below).
_help.surface: Design §FM.7 and §EW.7 step 2 (Claude Code, queue 71, 9 Oct; first guesses, Mike tunes by playing): the surface pocket above the tomb, its world's overworld (Surface). Take the stair up out of the dungeon and you come out at the ruin over it, day, dusk or night on the one clock; ambience only: nothing gated by the hour, nothing needed, nothing that hunts you; no map, no fast travel, no edge to another world. on: false keeps exit.stand_in for every dungeon. world: the worlds entry it is (desert, biome hot_desert). over_themes: the crawler.json themes whose dungeons have it above them; any other keeps exit.stand_in. realm: the biome's associations grown are this realm's (nearctic: the Sonoran and Chihuahuan ones). across_m: the basin's width (within size.across_m). ground: cell_m the grid (the ground and its collision), roll_m and roll_scale_m the floor's gentle roll, ripple_m and ripple_scale_m the wind's ripple on it, flat_round_stair_m [flat to, eased by] round the stairhead, pavement_share how much of the floor is darker gravel; wash (a dry watercourse out along the way out toward the landmark): from_m past the stairhead, width_m, depth_m, wander_m either side of its line, bank_m the banks its trees grow on (the bed itself stays open sand, no tree in it, so it runs out pale toward the landmark). edge (the land closes it, never an invisible wall): wander (the share of the radius the escarpment's line wanders), talus_width_m and talus_rise_m [lo, hi] (the walkable bajada under it), cliff_width_m and cliff_m [lo, hi] (the escarpment, always steeper than world_scale.json walk_max_deg), beyond_m (the plateau behind it, hidden behind the lip); landmark: a butte out_m past the cliff straight out along the way out, radius_m, height_m over the plateau. far_band: radius_m, height_m [lo, hi], segments: the far ranges in the haze, not walkable. sky: fog_day and fog_night (the haze a metre past fog_start_m; no far edge, the land closes the view), mist_place (the share of the look's low mist that lies here), cloud and wind_mps (fair weather, not simulated, §EW.6), camera_far_m (the view's reach up here; 400 below). plants: zones (the biome association grown on the wash and its banks, on the flats, and on the upland bajada within upland_from_edge_m of the cliff's foot), per_hectare (where an association's cover is 0.3; more where it covers more), dominant_share (the association's dominant species' share, §CS), ground_per_hectare and ground_within_m (its grasses and ferns, round the stairhead), near_m (each block's near meshes inside it, the impostors past it), clear_m (trees at least this far apart; a tree has a trunk you can't walk through). life: count [lo, hi] creatures, within_m [near, far] of you, one fallen further behind than gone_past_m back ahead. finds (§FG, never required): remains, camps and litter [lo, hi] each, within_m [near, far] of the stairhead, clear_of_stair_m, apart_m. stairhead: drop_m (how far its steps go down), half_m (the stair's half width), yard_m [along, across] (its yard of flags, at least the dip the stairwell's cut leaves round it), wall_m [lo, hi] (the yard's broken walls), down_at_m (how far down the steps the way down begins). stacks: smoke_scale (times smoke.json hearth.stack_scale), slot_m [long, wide] and soot_m (a flue's slot and its soot). arrive: fade_s (the dark each way), out_m (where you come out, past the portal), back_in_m (where you come in, inside the opening on the landing), log_up and log_down (the log's lines). sound: wind_db, day_db (cicadas by day), night_db (crickets by night). The surface is built the first time you go up, from the dungeon's own seed (the same land every time for this game, §FK.2), and kept as you left it while you are below; the dungeon is kept as you left it while you are up here. Nothing up here is saved: Continue still wakes you by the hearth below.
